newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia prepares new forex transactions bill.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia prepares new forex transactions bill.

text.p: The Slovenian government said on Thursday it had prepared legislation on foreign exchange transactions aimed at bringing the country's laws in line with European Union regulations.

"The bill will enable gradual liberalisation of foreign exchange transactions in line with (Slovenia's) association agreement with the EU," Andrej Simonic, state secretary at the Finance Ministry, told a news conference.
The association agreement was signed in June last year but has yet to be ratfied by Slovenia's parliament.

Simonic said the new bill, which is expected to be passed by parliament this year, would free foreign direct investment which currently needs government approval in the majority of cases. The bill would also provide clearer rules for foreign portfolio investors, he said.

According to the new law, international investors need to open fiduciary accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade in securities, while the balancing of foreign liabilities on the accounts will remain subject to Bank of Slovenia rules.

Since February, when the central bank said foreigners have to open such fiduciary accounts, foreign portfolio investment to Slovenia has all but stopped as international investors claim the costs of the accounts were too high.

Banks said the costs were so high because central bank rules obliged banks to balance foreign liabilities, including money paid into fiduciary accounts, against foreign assets. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
